claims.text: The simulated system is a single-crystal FeNiCrCoCu coating on a single-crystal Cu matrix.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has high lattice distortion.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating has a stable FCC structure at 300 K.
Nanoindentation is performed to 30 Å depth at 10 m/s at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K.
Above 900 K, thermal activation overcomes the lattice-distortion barrier.
Overcoming the lattice-distortion barrier causes rapid stacking-fault annihilation.
High-temperature deformation causes dislocation starvation.
Collapse of stacking faults and dislocation networks nucleates localized amorphous zones at the contact interface.
Loss of stacking-fault-energy stability at high temperature mediates the formation of transient amorphous zones.
Dislocation starvation causes a loss of strain-hardening capacity.
Accumulated plastic work combined with insufficient dislocation mobility causes local lattice disordering and amorphization.
The amorphous material replaces the load-bearing crystalline lattice with a low-shear-strength interfacial layer.
Formation and shear failure of the amorphous layer cause the friction-coefficient spike.
Formation and failure of the amorphous layer cause the loss of hardness and wear resistance.
At 900 K and 1200 K, friction rises sharply while hardness and wear resistance fall.
The high-temperature response includes an increase in HCP atom count from a transient phase transformation, followed by a spike in amorphous atom count.
At lower temperatures, partial-dislocation motion is hindered by lattice-scale friction.
At 300 K and 600 K, the material maintains crystalline integrity and high wear resistance.
A high initial density of stable stacking faults suppresses dislocation starvation.
Grain-boundary sliding is absent in the single-crystal configuration.

contradictions.description: The amorphous layer is described as having low shear strength and as a 'low-friction' layer, yet its formation is also asserted to cause a spike in the friction coefficient; no intermediate process is supplied to reconcile lower interfacial friction with higher measured friction.
The proposed cascade is stated to occur above 900 K, whereas the predicted outcome places the sharp transition at both 900 K and 1200 K. A strict 'above 900 K' threshold excludes 900 K.
